the relation between cell morphology and motor unit properties in a single motor pool.
the relation between motor unit type and the dimensions of motoneuron somata and stem processes.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the size of cat α‐motoneuron somata and stem‐dendrite diameters are related to motor unit force output and that the specific resistivities of the cell membranes of motoneurons are related to their conduction velocities.
cell size and stem dendrite number, but not soma diameter, are correlated with motor unit type and that this correlation is reflected in a systematic variation in the membrane area of the cell.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the dimensions of the soma and dendrites, as well as the specific resistivity, of the motoneurons of a muscle vary systematically with motor unit type.

the mean cell size of motoneurons supplying slow twitch muscle fibers is smaller than that of motoneurons innervating fast twitch muscle fibers, although considerable overlap exists between the distributions for the different unit types.

there is a tendency for the size of the soma and dendrites to decrease with motor unit type, and that this correlates with the conduction velocity, force output, and specific resistivity of cell membranes of the motoneurons.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in the cat, there is a systematic relation between cell size (AN) and motor unit type, but the relation is not a simple monotonic one.
